body:
Observed once, 2026-08-28, CI run 33186643825 attempt 1 (windows-latest, PR #495, a JSON-only diff): four failures in one run, every one a deadline. door-smoke's three browser stories each died at exactly the 30s CDP launch deadline. rails-guard-ci's unreadable-base case hit vitest's 30s test timeout at 86s wall - the gate subprocess crawled, the exit-code assertion never ran. Corroboration in the same run's GREEN tests: archive.test.ts spent 18016ms on a fixture case that took 353ms on the same platform earlier that day. The same files were green on windows in #494 minutes before and green again on the immediate rerun. Verdict: one pathologically slow runner, not four test defects.

The pattern to hold: when a windows red is a CLUSTER of distinct files all dying at round-number deadlines while unrelated tests crawl 10-50x, suspect the runner before any test. Check the run's neighboring test durations first - they are the free measurement.

Prior art, same organs: the CDP launch deadline was already raised once by ceremony (#343-#345); archive.test.ts already took a T180 weight reduction for windows load; T248 (archived) triaged the render-ocap and tutorial flakes with measurements.

Do NOT act on this ticket for a single recurrence of any ONE test - that test gets its own T248-style triage instead. Act if the CLUSTER shape recurs: then measure the runner (parallel file count, runner class, a timing canary) and consider pinning vitest's windows parallelism or a larger runner, which is an infra decision for Myk.

Acceptance criteria:
- (a) On a recurrence of the cluster shape, the run's duration profile is captured and compared to this ticket's numbers. Verify: numbers quoted in the follow-up PR or journal entry.
- (b) Any change is to CI infrastructure or vitest scheduling, never a widened per-test assertion or timeout. Verify: the diff of the closing PR.
title: Windows runner starvation reads as a flake cluster - hold the pattern, triage on recurrence
